market_summary: Markets are reeling from a post-midterm-election risk-off wave concentrated in US tech/AI names, with Nvidia -9.3% (Nov 5) and QQQ -6.5%/SPY -4.4% on fears that a Democratic-controlled Congress could tighten data-centre build-out regulation. Tesla added a company-specific shock, confirming it will wind down the failed Cybertruck program by mid-2027 after sales ran at ~10% of plan, sending the stock down nearly 11% intraday. In Singapore, bank earnings diverged sharply — OCBC beat with record banking profit while DBS and UOB missed, triggering a round of analyst target-price cuts and dragging the sector and the STI ETF lower. Broad volatility and elevated relative volumes across almost every name suggest nervous, headline-driven trading rather than orderly repricing, so near-term moves may overshoot in both directions.

picks.thesis: Tesla is killing the Cybertruck program by mid-2027 after it sold at roughly 10% of the planned 250k/year run-rate — a clear admission of a failed, capital-intensive product. The stock already dropped ~11% on the day, well beyond the broader market's -4% to -6% tech selloff, confirming this is idiosyncratic bad news, not just macro beta. High volatility (46% annualized) and beta of 1.76 mean further downside follow-through is plausible as analysts digest the write-down implications and refocus on Cybercab execution risk.
picks.news: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production by mid-2027 after Cybertruck sales reached only ~20,237 units in the US in 2025, vs a planned 250,000/year (2026-11-06).
picks.risks: Tesla's bulls focus on Cybercab/robotaxi optionality and a recent Barclays upgrade (Oct 26, target raised to 450); any positive FSD/robotaxi headline or short squeeze could reverse the move quickly given high short-covering risk in this highly volatile name.

picks.thesis: Nvidia fell 9.3% in a single session on fears that post-midterm political shifts could slow data-centre permitting/build-out, compounding an already steep downtrend (-23.5% in a month, -17.7% below its 50-day average). Rel. volume is nearly 3x normal, showing real distribution, not just noise. With earnings on Nov 17 acting as a binary catalyst into a jittery tape, momentum favors further weakness or at least continued high volatility before any policy clarity emerges.
picks.news: Nvidia shares fell 9.26% to $181.60 on Nov 5 amid a broad AI-chip selloff tied to data-centre regulation concerns following the midterm elections.
picks.risks: Analyst consensus remains overwhelmingly bullish (59 buys vs 3 non-buys, implied upside >80%), so this is a contrarian, momentum-only short; a dovish policy signal or strong Nov 17 earnings beat could trigger a sharp snap-back rally.

picks.thesis: UOB's Q3 results disappointed and prompted cautious 2027 guidance, and unlike DBS, there's no 'buying opportunity' framing from analysts — UOB's price action is weaker (-8.4% 1m, -12.5% 3m, below both 50- and 200-day averages) and the rating mix is the most cautious of the three banks (only 3 buys vs 11 holds). Elevated relative volume (1.98x) suggests continued distribution post-earnings.
picks.news: Analysts cut DBS and UOB target prices on Nov 6 after Q3 results missed, citing cautious 2027 guidance from bank management.
picks.risks: Consensus target still implies 18.5% upside, and a broader SGX bank-sector bounce (e.g., sympathy from an OCBC-led rally) could lift all three banks together regardless of UOB-specific weakness.

picks.thesis: OCBC was the standout among SG banks this earnings season, posting record banking operations profit (+16% YoY) and record 9M26 net profit, while DBS and UOB both missed and saw target cuts. OCBC's share price held up far better today (-0.7% vs -2.1% to -2.5% for peers), showing the market is already differentiating. With analyst consensus implying ~13% upside and a positive earnings surprise freshly priced in, OCBC looks like the relative-strength play within a weak sector.
picks.news: OCBC reported Q3 net profit of S$2.04bn, up 3% YoY, with record banking operations profit of S$1.90bn (+16%) and record 9M26 net profit of S$6.24bn (+10%), announced Nov 6.
picks.risks: OCBC is still down 14% from its 52-week high and trading below its 50-day average, so it remains exposed to broad SGX/bank-sector weakness and risk-off sentiment regardless of company-specific strength; a market-wide risk-off continuation could drag it down with peers.

picks.thesis: Berkshire is acting as a defensive haven amid the tech-led selloff — it's near its 52-week high (-1.2% from it) and up 13.1% over the past month even as SPY and QQQ fell sharply, reflecting low beta (0.36) and limited AI/data-centre exposure. With earnings due Nov 7, continued insurance/operating strength could reinforce this relative-strength trend as investors rotate out of high-beta tech into quality defensives.
picks.news: No company-specific catalyst reported; move reflects broad rotation away from AI/tech names amid the Nov 5-6 selloff (market_summary), with Berkshire reporting earnings Nov 7.
picks.risks: Consensus analyst target is actually slightly below current price (implied upside -2.9%, though coverage is thin with only 3 analysts), so this is a momentum/defensive-rotation thesis rather than a value call; a weak earnings print on Nov 7 or a broad market recovery that reignites risk appetite could stall the rally.
